messages.label: dispatch (no --root)
messages.note: CLI resolves the same OS-default store as user-started scheduler serve.

messages.label: same-ID replay: load saved context
messages.note: Reuse recorded selection; catalog edits do not change the task.

messages.label: pressure refusal: follow response
messages.note: No new ordinary task record is written. A supplied ID can still report unknown; do not infer absence or retry.

messages.label: if admitted: save task + Team context
preflight, then Start
messages.note: Guardian owns the scope and budget; runner executes.

messages.label: after closure: seal + finalize
messages.note: TaskDir evaluates sealed output and commits outcome.json.

messages.label: cancel ACTIVE_TASK_ID
messages.note: Separate path from B. Terminal tasks return unchanged.

messages.label: new task; same session
messages.note: Local continuation re-enters fresh admission with saved session and Team context, under allowed overrides.

messages.label: dispatch --device worker
messages.note: Remote alternative to A/B. Queue, execution, provider and task records below are on the destination.

messages.label: verified SSH: admit once
messages.note: Origin saves immutable intent and a before-send marker first. Destination validates identity and requires its persistent supervisor.

messages.label: execute B on destination
messages.note: Destination guardian owns the task budget and closure. SSH disconnect does not cancel it.

messages.label: created / unknown / refusal
messages.note: Origin caches a dated observation; it gains no terminal authority.

messages.label: result + observed connectivity
messages.note: A cached observation or downloaded output is not a new terminal authority.

cards.title: Local entries; one execution owner
items: Agent and manual commands omit --root and share one OS-default store across project directories. Plain user-started scheduler serve can be ready before the first definition. Its host and calendar are shown in the component map; a scheduled entry calls this lifecycle in process only after a new committed claim.

Optional Team selection reads current Member defaults before fresh admission. Every new scheduled occurrence resolves them anew; explicit caller choices stay authoritative and Roles grant no permissions (internal/app/teams_schedule_create.go:25–51).

Same-ID replay uses saved Team selection. Continuation inherits the recorded Team context, provider session and config under existing explicit caller override rules (internal/tasklifecycle/continuation_request.go:9–26).

cards.title: How to read the alternatives
items: A and B show a local request/completion path only when fresh admission succeeds. Pressure refuses new work before ordinary task-record creation; a caller-supplied ID can retain unknown/stop_and_report, so follow the returned guidance.
C is a separate active-task cancellation path, not a step after B has published a terminal outcome. D is an explicit new request after the predecessor ends.
For an intentional custom or historical root, preserve its exact --root for dispatch, reads, controls and continuation. Nothing moves existing task records.

cards.title: The result has one owner
items: The runner joins provider output and native closure, then seals output and asks TaskDir to finalize. TaskDir interprets sealed evidence and commits outcome.json (internal/execution/run.go:131–165).
A response carrying a task id alone does not establish task creation. Observe only a task_record: created response and follow its failure guidance.
Collection may reconcile existing saved evidence; it does not launch another provider turn (internal/tasklifecycle/collection.go:13–63).

cards.title: Cancellation and continuation
items: The active guardian handles native termination. If the task is idle, stopping the saved queue row requires its lifetime-owner lease; an acknowledgement alone does not prove closure (internal/tasklifecycle/stop/operation.go:18–103).
The new continuation task uses the saved provider session in the caller's current scope. A missing or incompatible session refuses continuation; it does not invent one.

cards.title: Optional Git isolation
items: This sequence shows the ordinary provider turn. Managed workspace preparation and capture are optional, with their own receipts (internal/workspaces/admission.go:16–62; capture.go:123–150).
Workspace capture requires its helper lifetime to close and remains independent of the task's terminal verdict.

cards.title: Remote transport does not own the task
items: E is a separate remote request, not a step after local continuation. Destination reuses A/B execution and C cancellation. The caller owns origin intent and observation records; destination TaskDir alone owns task state (internal/remote/reference.go:19–35,66–100,184–214).

A durable before-send marker prevents another admit after an uncertain transmission. Reconnection performs existing-only reconciliation under the same destination identity, not a provider restart (internal/remote/coordinator.go:24–103).

Remote cancellation is sent to the destination with its recorded request identity. Logs and continuation are unsupported for remote references; no local fallback or fresh dispatch is implied (internal/app/remotecommands/origin.go:255–283).
